then.text: Same pint, smaller pound. Write that in your little book.

else.text: Decimal Day, 15 February 1971. I was a lad. Twelve pence to the shilling, twenty shillings to the pound, gone in a weekend.
Two hundred and forty old pence became a hundred new ones. Folk swore the shops rounded everything up.
Then the seventies. In 1975 prices went up by about a quarter in one year. Wages chased them. Nobody caught anything.
That's inflation. The pint's the same pint. It's the pound that shrinks.
If prices rise 2% a year, what does a £5 pint cost in ten years?

then.text: Spot on. Two per cent on top of two per cent, ten times over. It compounds, like interest.

else.text: About £6.10. Two per cent on top of two per cent, ten times over. It compounds, like interest.
The Bank of England aims for 2% a year. In October 2022 it hit 11.1%. I noticed. My pint noticed.

whitelocks_quiz.text: {greeting} Oldest pub in Leeds, 1715. Quiz night every night if you ask nicely.

whitelocks_regular.text: {greeting} Pull up a stool. Them mirrors are older than my granddad. So's the beer, if you believe the landlord.
